tour.overview:
Zanzibar's Stone Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000, grew as the capital of the Omani sultans who ruled the coast in the 19th century, and as a hub of the Indian Ocean trade in spices, ivory and, tragically, enslaved people. Its architecture blends Swahili, Arab, Indian and European influences, with famous carved doors. The island's plantations made it the world's leading producer of cloves, and it is still known as the Spice Island.

This private day shows Stone Town, a spice farm and Prison Island with a licensed guide and a vehicle.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel on Zanzibar
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver; private boat to Prison Island
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Stone Town.
• The slave market memorial.
• Darajani market.
• A spice farm.
• Prison Island.
• Forodhani gardens.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide navigates the maze of Stone Town and tells its layered history, and the vehicle and boat link the town, the farm and the island.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, food lovers, families and couples.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the sea, choose our Mnemba snorkelling day.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Zanzibar is mainly Muslim: dress modestly in Stone Town, covering shoulders and knees. During Ramadan, avoid eating in public in daytime.

days.name: Stone Town, a spice farm, Prison Island and the Forodhani night market
days.description:
What to expect: Zanzibar's history, spices and tortoises, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, boat, entrances and lunch.

Your guide collects you at about 8:30. Your day begins with a spice farm in the countryside, where you walk among clove trees, nutmeg, cinnamon, cardamom, vanilla vines and pepper, taste tropical fruits and learn how spices are used in cooking and medicine, with a Swahili lunch cooked with them.

Back in Stone Town, you walk through the alleys, admiring the carved and brass-studded doors, and visit the slave market memorial, where the last open slave market in East Africa operated until 1873. The Anglican Christ Church Cathedral was built on its site, its altar where the whipping post stood; beneath it, you see the dark chambers where people were held. You see the Old Fort, the facade of the House of Wonders, the former sultan's palace, and Darajani market, with its fish, fruit and spices.

In the late afternoon, a private boat takes you to Prison Island, where Aldabra giant tortoises, some over a century old, roam freely. You return at sunset to the Forodhani gardens, where the night market serves grilled seafood, Zanzibar pizza and sugar-cane juice.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:30 – Spice farm.
12:00 – Swahili lunch.
13:30 – Stone Town walk.
14:30 – Slave market memorial and cathedral.
15:30 – Darajani market.
16:15 – Boat to Prison Island.
18:00 – Forodhani night market.
19:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Freddie Mercury’s birthplace is on the walk.
• A sunset dhow cruise can be added.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrances, spice farm and lunch, boat to Prison Island, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: night market food, tips.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a Swahili lunch at the spice farm.

faq.question: What should we wear in Stone Town?
faq.answer: Modest clothes covering shoulders and knees.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Stone Town’s alleys are narrow; the boat needs a step.

faq.question: Can we swim at Prison Island?
faq.answer: Yes, there is a small beach and snorkelling.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. The spice farm sells spices, with no obligation to buy.

faq.question: Is Zanzibar safe?
faq.answer: Yes; follow your guide’s advice and dress respectfully.

faq.question: Do we need vaccinations?
faq.answer: Check with your doctor; malaria prevention is recommended.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: June to October and December to February.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary on safari in Tanzania: guides, drivers and camp staff appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice. Your guide can suggest typical amounts.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
